Papers / Visual explanation

Give a robot a memory it doesn't have to curate.

Keep every stream, compress it as you go, and learn what to remember.

In the Cover Blocks task, red, green and blue blocks sit in a random order. The robot covers them left to right, then must uncover them in red, green, blue order. Once they're covered, every order looks the same, so how does the policy know which to open first? It has to remember. Most memory methods for vision-language-action (VLA) policies pick what to keep: recent frames, keyframes, text summaries, or a learned video-only summary. Imprint doesn't pick. It compresses the video, the robot's actions and its joint positions into 256 memory tokens, updated as the episode runs, so cost stays bounded. On RMBench's nine memory tasks, π0.5 goes from 25.4% to 72.8% success, the best of the memory methods compared and the fastest, at 122.8 ms per action chunk.

Stage 1 needs no policy or labels.
